text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said it had approved a merger of three Bulgarian privatised breweries, which hold a 20 percent stake of the local beer market. Belgium's Interbrew, which has acquired majority stakes in the three companies through sell-offs, will hold 67 percent in the new company. @
-- Bulgaria has asked the European Union Commission to lift its recent ban on Bulgarian dairy products exports to the EU, Agriculture Minister Ventsislav Varbanov said.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet is expected to set up a mechanism, allowing the State Savings Bank to extend preferential loans of up to 500,000 levs per year to university students to fund their education, deputy Prime minister Vesselin Metodiev said. @

-- Bulgaria's Association of Commercial Banks (ACB) urged the central bank to exclude German marks from its regulations on banks' net open foreign exchange positions because the mark could not be considered a risky exposure under the currency board system, which pegged the lev at 1,000 to the mark, ACB board chairman Ognyan Enchev said.

-- Japan's Mitsubishi Corp. was interested in mediating negotiations to provide a $100 million loan for an upgrade of Bulgaria's southeast Black Sea port of Bourgas, the port's executive director George Dereliev said.
-- Bulgaria's State Savings Bank said it had extended some 128.5 billion lev loans to fund purchasing of wheat from this year's crop.

-- Bulgaria's parliament approved on second and final reading a bill to open secret police files from the communist era. The opposition Socialist party walked out of the session and said they would appeal to the Constitutional Court because the bill contravened the country's constitution.

-- Bulgaria is expected to offer for floor trading packages of shares, including five to 10 percent equity of the state National Electricity Company, the chemical fertiliser maker Chimco and the cigarette maker Bulgartabak Holding, in the autumn when Bulgaria's new stock exchange is expected to launch operations, deputy Industry Minister Marin Marinov said.

-- Bulgarian private companies have imported 10,000 tonnes of Romanian wheat from this year's crop because of lower prices and imports of another 20,000 tonnes were expected to be finalised in the next few days, Bulgaria's Dobrudzha Commodity Exchange said. @
-- Bulgaria's police said it had seized some one million pirate CDs hidden in a Sofia house garage. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 4145
